## 0. What this notebook does differently

This is a variant of `DMS_analysis.Rmd` (see that notebook for the full
walkthrough of the experiment, the conditions, and the basic logic - it's
not repeated here). The difference is in how it handles something that
notebook's library-complexity check (Section 2) turned up: in this pool, a
handful of binders dominate the read counts in every sample, while most of
the other ~80 are read-starved by comparison. Because every binder's count
is really a *share* of a fixed sequencing total, those dominant
(high-expressing) binders distort the normalisation for everyone else - even
a binder whose own abundance didn't really change can look enriched or
depleted just because the dominant clones' share shifted around it.

**The fix here**: identify the high-expressing binders and exclude them
before normalising - the comparison then runs only on the remaining
low-expressing binders, so their frequencies are computed against their own
total, never diluted by the dominant clones' reads. The high-expressing
binders themselves aren't analysed or reported on here at all - they're only
used to decide what to exclude.

**What this does and doesn't fix**: excluding the dominant clones removes a
real normalisation distortion. It does *not* manufacture extra sequencing
depth - a binder with genuinely few reads still has genuinely few reads.

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
```

## 1. Load data

```{r load-data}
counts_long <- read_tsv("../results/binder_counts.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
samples     <- read_tsv("../config/samples.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)

counts_long <- counts_long %>%
  complete(binder_id, sample_id = samples$sample_id, fill = list(count = 0)) %>%
  left_join(samples %>% select(sample_id, condition, ara_pct, iptg_mM),
            by = "sample_id")

head(counts_long)
```

## 2. QC: sequencing depth, library complexity, viability

Same QC as `DMS_analysis.Rmd` - included here so the exclusion step below
has a clean, already-filtered starting point.

```{r qc-depth}
depth <- counts_long %>%
  group_by(sample_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(total_reads = sum(count), n_binders_detected = sum(count > 0), .groups = "drop")

depth %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(sample_id, total_reads), y = total_reads, fill = condition)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Total usable read pairs", title = "Sequencing depth per sample") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r qc-table}
depth
```

### Library complexity: how evenly is the pool represented?

```{r library-complexity}
complexity <- counts_long %>%
  group_by(sample_id, condition) %>%
  mutate(sample_total = sum(count)) %>%
  arrange(sample_id, desc(count)) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number(), cum_share = cumsum(count) / sample_total) %>%
  ungroup()

complexity %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rank, y = cum_share, group = sample_id, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.9, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Binders, ranked by abundance (most abundant first)",
       y = "Cumulative share of reads",
       title = "Library complexity per sample",
       subtitle = "A steep early climb to the dashed line (90%) means a handful of binders dominate the pool") +
  theme_minimal()
```

This is exactly the pattern that motivates excluding the high-expressing
binders below - if it's flat/gradual here (no dominant clones), that
exclusion step won't change much and you may as well use the unsplit
`DMS_analysis.Rmd` instead.

### Viability filter: drop binders that don't survive no-inducer selection

```{r viability-filter}
min_no_inducer_reads <- 10  # tune by eye against the histogram below

no_inducer_counts <- counts_long %>%
  filter(condition == "no_inducer") %>%
  select(binder_id, no_inducer_count = count)

no_inducer_counts %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = no_inducer_count)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = min_no_inducer_reads, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "no_inducer read count", y = "Number of binders",
       title = "Choosing the viability threshold",
       subtitle = paste("Dashed line: current threshold =", min_no_inducer_reads)) +
  theme_minimal()

dead_binders <- no_inducer_counts %>%
  filter(no_inducer_count < min_no_inducer_reads) %>%
  pull(binder_id)

if (length(dead_binders) > 0) {
  message(length(dead_binders), " binder(s) dropped as non-viable (no_inducer count < ",
          min_no_inducer_reads, "): ", paste(dead_binders, collapse = ", "))
} else {
  message("No binders dropped - all binders survive no-inducer selection above threshold.")
}

counts_long <- counts_long %>% filter(!(binder_id %in% dead_binders))
```

### Identifying the high-expressing binders to exclude

Rank binders by their overall abundance (mean raw read count across *all*
samples and conditions - not just one condition, since Section 2's library
complexity check showed the same handful of binders dominate every
condition about equally). Binders at or above the threshold are
high-expressing and get excluded from here on; everyone else is
low-expressing and carries through to the actual analysis.

```{r expression-batch-split}
high_expr_threshold <- 1000  # mean read count across all samples; tune by eye against the histogram below

overall_abundance <- counts_long %>%
  group_by(binder_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_count_overall = mean(count), .groups = "drop")

overall_abundance %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_count_overall)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_number()) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = high_expr_threshold, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Mean read count across all samples (log scale)", y = "Number of binders",
       title = "Choosing the high/low expression split",
       subtitle = paste("Dashed line: current threshold =", high_expr_threshold)) +
  theme_minimal()

expr_batch <- overall_abundance %>%
  mutate(batch = if_else(mean_count_overall >= high_expr_threshold, "high", "low"))

high_expr_binders <- expr_batch %>% filter(batch == "high") %>% pull(binder_id)
low_expr_binders  <- expr_batch %>% filter(batch == "low") %>% pull(binder_id)

message(length(high_expr_binders), " high-expressing binder(s) excluded, ",
        length(low_expr_binders), " low-expressing binder(s) carried through to the analysis.")

# Sanity check: the excluded high-expressing binders should hold most of the
# READS despite being few in number - that mismatch is why excluding them
# matters for the low-expressing binders' own normalisation.
counts_long %>%
  left_join(expr_batch %>% select(binder_id, batch), by = "binder_id") %>%
  group_by(batch) %>%
  summarise(n_binders = n_distinct(binder_id), total_reads = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(share_of_reads = total_reads / sum(total_reads))

counts_long <- counts_long %>% filter(binder_id %in% low_expr_binders)
```

## 3. Normalisation

Same as `DMS_analysis.Rmd` Section 3, but normalising only sees the
low-expressing binders from here on - the high-expressing binders excluded
above never enter the total that frequencies are computed against.

```{r normalise}
pseudocount <- 1

counts_norm <- counts_long %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  mutate(
    total_reads = sum(count),
    freq        = (count + pseudocount) / (total_reads + pseudocount * n_distinct(counts_long$binder_id))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

condition_freq <- counts_norm %>%
  select(condition, binder_id, freq)

condition_freq %>% head()
```

## 4. Innate toxicity of overexpression (reference only)

```{r innate-toxicity}
baseline <- condition_freq %>%
  filter(condition == "no_inducer") %>%
  select(binder_id, baseline_freq = freq)

innate_toxicity <- condition_freq %>%
  filter(condition %in% c("library_only_0.1mM", "library_only_1mM")) %>%
  left_join(baseline, by = "binder_id") %>%
  mutate(log2FC = log2(freq / baseline_freq))

innate_toxicity %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = binder_id, y = log2FC)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~condition, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Binder", y = "log2FC vs. no_inducer",
       title = "Innate toxicity of overexpression (no toxin present)",
       subtitle = "Reference only - not used in the hit-calling comparison below") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

## 5. The actual question: toxin+library vs. library-only (matched IPTG level)

Both arms here have the binder induced at the same IPTG level, so each
binder's own overexpression cost is present on both sides of the ratio and
should mostly cancel out - what's left over is mainly the effect of adding
the toxin on top of an already-expressed binder.

```{r key-comparison}
library_only_freq <- condition_freq %>%
  filter(condition %in% c("library_only_0.1mM", "library_only_1mM")) %>%
  mutate(iptg_level = str_remove(condition, "library_only_")) %>%
  select(binder_id, iptg_level, library_only_freq = freq)

key_comparison <- condition_freq %>%
  filter(condition %in% c("toxin_plus_library_0.1mM", "toxin_plus_library_1mM")) %>%
  mutate(iptg_level = str_remove(condition, "toxin_plus_library_")) %>%
  left_join(library_only_freq, by = c("binder_id", "iptg_level")) %>%
  mutate(log2FC = log2(freq / library_only_freq)) %>%
  select(-iptg_level)

key_comparison %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(binder_id, log2FC), y = log2FC, fill = condition)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Binder", y = "log2FC vs. library-only (same IPTG level)",
       title = "Enrichment of each binder when co-induced with toxin",
       subtitle = "Positive = binder does better under toxin challenge than its own baseline without toxin") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Caveat:** this assumes each binder's own overexpression cost is about the
same with or without toxin present, and isn't a substitute for a true GFP
(neutral-overexpression) control, which the plate-based version of this
assay uses and we don't have here. Cross-check any top hit against the
innate toxicity plot above and against the 0.1 mM vs. 1 mM dose response (a
true binder should show *more* protection at higher induction).

## 6. Final ranked hit table

```{r final-hits}
hit_results <- key_comparison %>%
  select(binder_id, condition, log2FC) %>%
  arrange(condition, desc(log2FC))

hit_results
```

```{r final-plot}
hit_results %>%
  filter(condition == "toxin_plus_library_1mM") %>%
  slice_max(log2FC, n = 20) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(binder_id, log2FC), y = log2FC)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Binder", y = "log2FC vs. library-only (1 mM IPTG)",
       title = "Top 20 RcaT binders by protection") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r save-final-table}
write_csv(hit_results, "../results/final_binder_ranking_low_expressing.csv")
```

## 7. Comparison to the published plate-based screen (Sen2 retron)

Same reference data and same caveats as `DMS_analysis.Rmd` Section 7 (their
effect size uses an IPTG-low baseline and a GFP correction we don't have -
this is a rough sanity check, not a strict validation).

```{r load-plate-reference}
plate_reference <- read_tsv("../data/plate_assay_reference_hits.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(retron == "Sen2") %>%
  transmute(genename, plate_pval = pval, plate_log2_efsize = log2(efsize), plate_hit = hit)

# Our binder_id values carry a naming-scheme prefix (`result_...` or
# `rcat-binder-..._result_<n>`) that the collaborator's gene names don't -
# strip it down to the same bare name before joining.
binder_name_map <- tibble(binder_id = unique(hit_results$binder_id)) %>%
  mutate(
    genename = binder_id %>%
      str_remove("^rcat-binder-") %>%
      str_remove("^result_") %>%
      str_replace("_result_", "_")
  )

comparison <- hit_results %>%
  left_join(binder_name_map, by = "binder_id") %>%
  left_join(plate_reference, by = "genename") %>%
  filter(!is.na(plate_log2_efsize))

comparison %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = plate_log2_efsize, y = log2FC, colour = plate_hit)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~condition) +
  labs(x = "Published plate assay: log2(effect size), Sen2 (vs. IPTG-low)",
       y = "This screen: log2FC (toxin+library vs. library-only, matched IPTG)",
       title = "This screen (low-expressing binders) vs. the published plate-based assay",
       colour = "Plate-assay hit call") +
  theme_minimal()

comparison %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    pearson_r         = cor(log2FC, plate_log2_efsize, use = "complete.obs"),
    n_binders_matched = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r save-comparison-table}
write_csv(comparison, "../results/plate_assay_comparison_low_expressing.csv")
```

A positive correlation here is reassuring, but don't over-read a weak one:
this screen's baseline (library-only, matched IPTG) and the plate assay's
(IPTG-low, GFP-corrected) aren't quite the same comparison, both assays have
their own noise, and a binder missing from `plate_reference` above just
wasn't in that dataset.

Compare this correlation against `DMS_analysis.Rmd`'s unsplit
`plate_assay_comparison.csv` - if it's noticeably better here, that's
evidence the high-expressing binders really were distorting the comparison
for everyone else, which is exactly the problem excluding them is meant to
fix. If it's about the same, the remaining binders' own read depth (not the
high-expressing binders' compositional pull) is the limiting factor.

## Where to go from here

* If almost every binder lands in the high-expressing group (or almost none
  do), the `high_expr_threshold` in Section 2 is in the wrong place for this
  dataset - move it and re-knit; the histogram there is the thing to look
  at, not a fixed number.
* Everything in `DMS_analysis.Rmd`'s own "Where to go from here" still
  applies here too (the dose-response check and the missing GFP control).
